title: 29 U.S.C. § 794 — Rehabilitation Act Section 504: Nondiscrimination Under Federal Grants
enacting_law: Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Pub. L. 93-112, § 504, 87 Stat. 394
major_amendments: Civil Rights Restoration Act of 1987, Pub. L. 100-259 — institution-wide coverage; Grove City reversal
ADA Amendments Act of 2008, Pub. L. 110-325 — disability definition amendments incorporated via § 794(d)
verified_note: USC tool returned 'not found' for Title 29 § 794. Text from training knowledge. STEWARD MUST VERIFY full text at uscode.house.gov → Title 29 → Chapter 16 → § 794 before citing in federal court filings.
case_application: DDS (federally-funded disability determinations) — phantom contact fraud + fabricated records; CalVCB (VOCA-funded) — disability discrimination in claims process; Blue Shield/hospitals (Medicare/Medicaid-funded) — denial of medically necessary care to disabled person. CRRA ensures institution-wide coverage: if any program receives federal funds, all programs of that entity are covered.
key_cases: Grove City College v. Bell, 465 U.S. 555 (1984) — narrowed §504 to program-specific coverage; SUPERSEDED by CRRA (1987)
Civil Rights Restoration Act of 1987 (Pub. L. 100-259) — Congress restored institution-wide coverage; Grove City legislative reversal
solely_standard_note: §794's 'solely by reason of disability' causation is textually stricter than ADA's 'on the basis of disability' but courts apply ADA standards in most circuits after § 794(d) incorporation of ADA Title I for employment; for program access claims, 'solely' has been narrowed by judicial interpretation
unruh_per_se: CIV § 51(f) — ADA violation = per se Unruh violation; §794(d) incorporates ADA standards into §504; therefore §504 violation → ADA standard violated → §51(f) per se → $4,000 minimum statutory damages in California court
